item.title: Patrick Mahomes Sounds Alarm on Jalen Hurts Health Scare in NFL
item.description: Patrick Mahomes has kept his focus sharp this season. The Chiefs improved to 5-0 after a 22-6 win over the Chargers on Sunday, and the quarterback now has a lot to say off the field. His latest comments address a serious health scare involving fellow Eagles star Jalen Hurts , and they carry real weight around the league. Patrick Mahomes Sounds Alarm on Jalen Hurts Health Scare in NFL Mahomes addressed the situation on 96.5 The Fan podcast after the Eagles confirmed that Jalen Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and clots in both lungs. Hurts was first diagnosed with a superficial clot in his calf in London on Oct. 10, then played in the 19-17 loss to the Jaguars. The Eagles later ruled him out of Week 6 and placed him on injured reserve. Reports say he will miss the rest of the season. The team and his agent, Nicole Lynn, said he is clinically stable and expects a full recovery. Feb 9, 2025; New Orleans, LA, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) greets Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) following Super Bowl LIX at Ceasars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images “I mean, it’s extremely scary,” Mahomes said. “I mean that it comes from, I guess, a cleat or something like that. I don’t know all the details, but that’s something that happens every single week in the NFL.” Mahomes did not know every detail, but noted that Hurts rarely misses games, which makes a life-threatening clot even harder to process. He added that the news puts football in perspective, since players are human beings with families. Meanwhile, Mahomes was glad doctors found the clots now so Hurts can start treatment, and he hopes the quarterback returns to the field. “So luckily they were able to kind of get it found out now what it actually is and he can get on the medication or whatever it is that he needs to be on and and hopefully he can get back on that field again cuz the NFL’s better when you have great players on it and he’s one of those players.” Hurts will need blood thinners for at least three months, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Mahomes was not the only voice in the story, and questions about the Eagles and their medical decisions are growing. Eagles Face Scrutiny Over Decision to Clear Jalen Hurts for London Game The Eagles are also dealing with pressure from outside the locker room. Their statement said an ultrasound after the team’s flight to London showed a superficial clot, and doctors there concluded Hurts could safely play. He completed 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown against Jacksonville. On Monday, coach Nick Sirianni declined to explain why the team allowed Hurts to fly home with the clot, according to the Associated Press. Several analysts also questioned whether Hurts should have played on little rest. Tanner McKee has taken over under center. He threw for 215 yards and a touchdown in a 25-14 loss to the Panthers, which dropped Philadelphia to 2-4 and extended its losing streak to four g

item.title: Former Barcelona defender explains why Flick’s side have the edge over Real Madrid: ‘Not a normal match’
item.description: Former Barcelona defender explains why Flick’s side have the edge over Real Madrid: ‘Not a normal match’ Former Barcelona left-back Sergi Barjuan believes Hansi Flick’s side have the advantage over Real Madrid ahead of Sunday’s El Clasico at Spotify Camp Nou, pointing to their recent form, fitness and tactical structure as reasons to favour the Catalans. However, Barjuan has also warned that the rivalry rarely follows ordinary footballing logic, with Real Madrid arriving after a strong Champions League result and renewed confidence ahead of one of the season’s biggest fixtures. Barjuan also expressed frustration with the growing off-field tension surrounding the Clasico , arguing that discussions in boardrooms and the media have threatened to overshadow the contest itself. Sergi Barjuan believes Barcelona have the edge over Real Madrid Barjuan expects a closely contested match but sees Barcelona as the stronger side based on their current performances. The former defender acknowledged Madrid’s recent progress while suggesting that Flick’s team have shown greater consistency in several important areas. “Barça are in very good form. The statistics speak for themselves. But we’re talking about a Clasico, and a Clasico isn’t a normal match. “Real Madrid are coming off the back of a good win in the Champions League and have been strengthened, but in terms of structure, fitness and results, I see Barça as the better side.” Barjuan criticises off-field Clasico tensions Sergi Barjuan has backed Hansi Flick’s Barcelona. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) Beyond his prediction, Barjuan lamented the extent to which the build-up has focused on disputes away from the pitch. He believes the players should determine the narrative through their performances rather than become secondary figures in a wider exchange between the clubs. “Honestly, it would be great if the talk were solely about football and the spectacle. The players should do their talking on the pitch,” he said. Barjuan subsequently pointed to disagreements over refereeing decisions and accused those involved of being selective about which incidents receive attention. He also referenced Jose Mourinho, suggesting that people involved in football naturally defend their own interests. “Everyone has the right to express their opinion and judge as they see fit. Barça are speaking on the pitch. And that’s where you see the differences between the two teams. “There have been refereeing controversies and they’ve tried to sweep them under the carpet. They don’t see the footage when they don’t want to see it. And vice versa. Barcelona lost to PSG but are still favourites to beat Real Madrid. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) “We know Mourinho well enough; everyone looks out for their own interests. I know him personally and I know what he’s made of,” he added. item.title: 'Not what a captain should be' - the debate around Fernandes' outburst
item.description: Bruno Fernandes' comments after Manchester United's humbling by Como have got fans and pundits talking - but what now for the captain? United's 4-1 Champions League defeat in Italy was the result of a wretched performance and Fernandes questioned boss Michael Carrick's tactics. "It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confidence," said the Portugal attacking midfielder on TNT Sports. Asked if Carrick got his tactics wrong, the 32-year-old continued: "That's on the manager and staff to see it, not me." Are these the actions of a captain? Fernandes rounds on Carrick after Man Utd humiliation Man Utd humbling by Como leaves Carrick job in danger Not according to former Liverpool vice-captain Jamie Carragher, working as a summariser, on CBS Sports. "He's reacted like that because he's been embarrassed by the manager [who] brought him off," said the ex-England defender. "And when he talks about pressing, whether it's man-to-man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can't press because he does things for the crowd. "He runs all over the place like a kid in the schoolyard for the supporters. They all think he's working hard. He's not. He's killing the rest of the team doing it." He added: "Watching him throw his arms up every week in a game is an absolute disgrace [and] calling the manager out considering how he's performed this season on the pitch. "[It's an] awful attitude and not what a Manchester United captain should be." Fernandes' comments come a week after defender Lisandro Martinez made similar headlines following United's previous Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid. item.content:encoded: Bruno Fernandes' comments after Manchester United's humbling by Como have got fans and pundits talking - but what now for the captain? United's 4-1 Champions League defeat in Italy was the result of a wretched performance and Fernandes questioned boss Michael Carrick's tactics. "It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confidence," said the Portugal attacking midfielder on TNT Sports. Asked if Carrick got his tactics wrong, the 32-year-old continued: "That's on the manager and staff to see it, not me." Are these the actions of a captain? Fernandes rounds on Carrick after Man Utd humiliation Man Utd humbling by Como leaves Carrick job in danger Not according to former Liverpool vice-captain Jamie Carragher, working as a summariser, on CBS Sports. "He's reacted like that because he's been embarrassed by the manager [who] brought him off," said the ex-England defender. "And when he talks about pressing, whether it's man-to-man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can't press because he does things for the crowd. "He runs all over the place like a kid in the schoolyard for the supporters. They all think he's working hard. He's not. He's killing the rest of the team doing it." He added: "Watching him throw his arms up every week in a game is an absolute disgrace [and] calling the manager out considering how he's performed this season on the pitch. "[It's an] awful attitude and not what a Manchester United captain should be." Fernandes' comments come a week after defender Lisandro Martinez made similar headlines following United's previous Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid. The Argentine said he expected more investment in the squad and "more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]". He later apologised. And while Martinez's outburst sparked debate, Fernandes' comments could have even larger repercussions. Carrick, who was under huge pressure already following a terrible start to the season, said in reply: "There's a little bit of whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win." United have not won in their past seven games since beating Champions League minnows Sabah. They have just one win in their seven Premier League games this season. 'He should not be saying these things' Not many people have defended Fernandes' public questioning of the tactics. But some do understand his frustrations. Former Leicester and Celtic keeper Kasper Schmeichel, whose dad Peter won the Champions League, five Premier League titles and three FA Cups as a United player, said on BBC Radio 5 Live: "Given last week and what's happened, he probably should not be saying these things because it's only going to add to the problems. "With experience you learn that you need to keep these things in-house. It's a problem, with everything that happened during the week. "Michael Carrick didn't need this, the club didn't need this. It's exposing all of the issues that are at Manchester United. "It's very plain to see that there are loads of issues but you need to be fixing them, you need to be having meetings within the club, which I'm sure that they are, but it's obviously not resolved. It's just translating on to the pitch." The issue that most pundits have is not that Fernandes has these opinions - but that he has let the world know them. Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock, speaking on BBC Match of the Day, said: "I think there will be ex-players now from Manchester United saying, 'why are you letting this get out, this should be a collective in the changing room where we come together'. "Whether you like the manager or not, you've got to come together and say 'OK how do we correct this?' "Senior players go to the manager and say 'listen we didn't agree with the tactics, we didn't think we got it right, how do we go about this, how do we move forward', because you start airing it in public and it doesn't end well for anyone." Former Chelsea midfielder Joe Cole on TNT Sports called it "sacrilege". "I've played for managers where I don't agree with the tactics but you might say that to your mate or to your wife. You don't come out as captain of the club and question the manager," he said. What do the fans think? Andy Mitten, editor of United We Stand, told BBC 5 Live Breakfast that Fernandes has "thrown his coach under the bus". "It's a terrible look," he continued. "And Manchester United fans are divided as to whether he should or should not do that. Last week, Martinez was also critical. A lot of Manchester United fans agreed with him. "Again, there's mitigation, he wants a new contract. That's because he's not been playing enough, because he's been injured. And injuries are a real problem for Manchester United. There's no recognised centre-forward. So it is a really difficult time for United." Former United midfielder Carrick, who took over in January initially as caretaker manager, seemed to blank his players at full-time before heading over to the United fans. "I don't blame him for ignoring the players," said Mitten. "He went to the fans and he held his hands up and he said, 'I'm sorry'. "You can tell he's hurting. He's a Manchester United fan himself. He was a season ticket holder only a year ago before he took the job. I think he's trying his best, but it's just not working at the moment. Manchester United are really, really struggling." What now for Fernandes? Bruno Fernandes has been United's captain for three years [Getty Images] Fernandes has been Manchester United's one consistent outstanding player since a £47m move from Sporting in January 2020, when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was the manager. He has scored 111 goals and made 106 assists in 338 games for the club in all competitions. Former manager Erik ten Hag made him the skipper in the summer of 2023 after taking the armband off Harry Maguire, whose place in the team was far from certain. But this is not the first time his body language, attitude and behaviour as captain has been criticised. He was called a "disgrace" and "embarrassing" by United legends Gary Neville and Roy Keane after the 7-0 loss to Liverpool in 2023, while Chris Sutton said he should never captain the club again. However, last season Fernandes was named the Premier League's player of the year after a record 21 assists in a season. "That award was on the back of Michael Carrick becoming the manager," said Carragher. "He wouldn't have got that award without Michael Carrick, because Michael Carrick put him back in his rightful position and he then went on to have a fantastic season because he's a talented footballer. "But in terms of attitude and the way he goes about things, it's not right at all." Fernandes has made headlines with his comments before. In August 2025 he said the club needed to make more signings. That December he was asked about the fact United had been willing to sell him to Al-Hilal and told Canal 11: "From the club I felt it was, 'If you go it's not so bad for us'. It hurts me a bit. "More than hurting me, it makes me sad. I'm a player that no-one can criticise, I'm always available, I always give my best. "I could have left in this transfer window, I would have earned much more money. "I would have won many trophies this season, but I decided not to go, not only for family reasons but because I genuinely love the club." But now the narrative might change entirely after his latest comments. Many will be wondering whether he should even start in Sunday's game against Bournemouth. Martinez did keep his place, after apologising, at Leeds last Sunday. But as United fan Mitten says: ''There was mitigation with Martinez because he wants a new contract. Fernandes is captain." item.title: Raptors send frightening early message with 43-point destruction of Bulls
item.description: Raptors send frightening early message with 43-point destruction of Bulls originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Toronto Raptors could hardly have imagined a more convincing beginning to the 2026-27 NBA season. Toronto overwhelmed the Chicago Bulls 135-92 on Wednesday night, delivering a 43-point victory that immediately generated excitement about the team's potential. The Raptors controlled the game with aggressive defense, perimeter shooting and contributions from several key players. Scottie Barnes finished with 23 points, six rebounds and five assists. Kawhi Leonard also scored 23 points, adding six assists and four steals in his first regular-season appearance since returning to Toronto. The win provided an encouraging opening statement for a franchise hoping to become a serious factor in the Eastern Conference. It also exposed significant problems for Chicago. Kawhi Leonard's return provides early excitement Leonard's return to the Raptors was one of the NBA's most intriguing offseason developments. The veteran forward previously helped Toronto win the 2019 NBA championship, earning Finals MVP honors during that historic run. His return gives the Raptors another experienced player capable of contributing on both ends of the floor. "I'm just going to play hard and try to have fun out there, and try to make the city proud." Kawhi (23 PTS, 6 REB, 4 STL) on his Raptors return 👏 https://t.co/YbRECRgJ0q — NBA (@NBA) October 22, 2026 Wednesday's performance was not perfect. Leonard made five of his 17 field-goal attempts, demonstrating that his offensive efficiency still has room for improvement. However, he found other ways to influence the game. His six assists helped Toronto maintain offensive movement, while his four steals contributed to a dominant defensive performance. Barnes also delivered an encouraging effort. The versatile forward made eight of 19 shots and showed the scoring ability that could become even more important with Leonard alongside him. Together, the two provide Toronto with an intriguing combination of size, playmaking and defensive versatility. MORE : Clippers get unexpected opening-night statement from Darius Garland after chaotic offseason Chicago suffers miserable offensive performance The Bulls entered the season hoping to establish chemistry with a reshaped roster. Their opening game offered few encouraging signs. Josh Giddey endured a particularly difficult evening, scoring just two points on 1-of-10 shooting. RJ Barrett helped set the defensive tone for Toronto, making life difficult for Chicago's primary ballhandler. The Bulls also struggled without center Nic Claxton, leaving them vulnerable around the basket. Toronto took advantage of those problems while building a commanding lead. By the final minutes, the outcome was no longer in doubt. The Raptors were able to finish the game comfortably as their home crowd celebrated an impressive opening

item.title: Joel Klatt reveals Big Ten-SEC scheduling plan for when playoff increases to 24 teams
item.description: A 24-team College Football Playoff has has been all but confirmed as starting as soon as next season, and there’s been no shortage of criticism for what feels like a largely unnecessary move. TT Big Ten and SEC, the primary driving force behind the College Football Playoff expansion push, have more plans in the works for when the expansion is finally ratified, per Fox’s Joel Klatt. “There are scheduling agreements that are in place once this thing expands officially,” Klatt told KTCK-FM 96.7 The Ticket in Dallas on Wednesday, per Football Scoop. “The next thing that will happen almost immediately is we’re going to get scheduling agreements between the SEC and the Big Ten; top-end matchups, mid-tier matchups, low-end matchups — and we’re going to be expanding the valuable matchups in the non-conference, far surpassing what we have now.” Big Ten commissioner Tony Petititi guaranteed earlier this month that with playoff expansion the conference would commit to a minimum of 10 Power 4 games. “We need to play more good games. I think we’ve been really clear about that. We think that the season can start way better than it does. We’re committed to that. If we get to a 24-team Playoff, you are going to see many more competitive games scheduled,” he said. However, as many grand plans as the Big Ten and SEC may have in the works, there will undoubtedly also be plenty of unintended consequences, even for the sport’s two premier conferences, and ESPN’s Dan Wetzel has already predicted a massive one that may lead each to regret pushing for the expansion. “Notre Dame now has the best situation in all of football – almost 100 percent guarantee to make the playoff, freedom to schedule as it wishes, maximization of its own media value,” he wrote on X. “To use the Big Ten as an example, why wouldn’t Ohio State, Michigan and Penn State follow? If you can, be independent. That’s the future,” he continued. “The 18-team Big Ten is bloated, distant, and winning it carries little intrinsic or competitive value for the biggest brands. “Those three schools can create a scheduling agreement that would increase their media revenue 2-3x and give the same control over everything. No sharing money. No forced TV times. Eight or even nine home games. Select your own schedule. Staying in the Big Ten now makes little and perhaps no economic sense.” College football will change substantially once playoff expansion officially passes. Only time will tell exactly what all of that change looks like. The post Joel Klatt reveals Big Ten-SEC scheduling plan for when playoff increases to 24 teams appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: The Timberwolves Just Gave Their Critics Something to Explain
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Timberwolves were supposed to have a problem with teams built like the Miami Heat. After trading Julius Randle and Naz Reid, Minnesota entered the season with understandable questions about its size, rebounding and ability to withstand physical opponents. A faster offense sounded exciting. Finding enough muscle around Rudy Gobert looked considerably less certain. Then the Wolves opened against Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo — and won the rebounding battle by 14. Anthony Edwards’ 45 points will dominate the conversation after Minnesota’s 131–106 victory Wednesday night. LaMelo Ball’s debut supplied plenty of highlights, too. But the most encouraging numbers for anyone worried about this roster might be found elsewhere in the box score . Minnesota finished with 52 rebounds to Miami’s 38. The offensive-rebounding margin was even more striking: 17–4. One game cannot settle a season-long concern. It can, however, complicate the assumption that the new Wolves will be easy to push around. The Timberwolves had been preparing for this test Oct 8, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo (7) dribbles the basketball against the New Orleans Pelicans during the first quarter at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Miami offered an immediate examination of Minnesota’s new identity. Antetokounmpo and Adebayo can attack with size, speed and power, forcing defenders to absorb contact while remaining disciplined. The Wolves knew what was coming. According to Edwards, they had spent much of the offseason preparing each other for precisely that kind of challenge. “If you see how we’ve been playing against each other for the past two months, then you’ll know we’re ready for physical teams,” Edwards said in his postgame interview . “We’ve been going at each other for the last two months. So it felt good to go put it on somebody else.” Ball offered a specific example of that daily pressure, pointing to Ayo Dosunmu’s willingness to defend the length of the floor. “With Ayo picking up full court every day,” Ball said, describing the team’s preparation in his postgame presser . “You’ve got a lot of players on the team just going at each other, for real.” That is useful context for a group whose offseason has often been discussed in terms of pace, shooting and personality. Finch saw another benefit from those sessions: players arrived ready to work. “I’ve never been around a team that we didn’t have to worry about getting anyone in shape this preseason,” he noted after the game. item.content:encoded: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Timberwolves were supposed to have a problem with teams built like the Miami Heat. After trading Julius Randle and Naz Reid, Minnesota entered the season with understandable questions about its size, rebounding and ability to withstand physical opponents. A faster offense sounded exciting. Finding enough muscle around Rudy Gobert looked considerably less certain. Then the Wolves opened against Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo — and won the rebounding battle by 14. Anthony Edwards’ 45 points will dominate the conversation after Minnesota’s 131–106 victory Wednesday night. LaMelo Ball’s debut supplied plenty of highlights, too. But the most encouraging numbers for anyone worried about this roster might be found elsewhere in the box score . Minnesota finished with 52 rebounds to Miami’s 38. The offensive-rebounding margin was even more striking: 17–4. One game cannot settle a season-long concern. It can, however, complicate the assumption that the new Wolves will be easy to push around. The Timberwolves had been preparing for this test Oct 8, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo (7) dribbles the basketball against the New Orleans Pelicans during the first quarter at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Miami offered an immediate examination of Minnesota’s new identity. Antetokounmpo and Adebayo can attack with size, speed and power, forcing defenders to absorb contact while remaining disciplined. The Wolves knew what was coming. According to Edwards, they had spent much of the offseason preparing each other for precisely that kind of challenge. “If you see how we’ve been playing against each other for the past two months, then you’ll know we’re ready for physical teams,” Edwards said in his postgame interview . “We’ve been going at each other for the last two months. So it felt good to go put it on somebody else.” Ball offered a specific example of that daily pressure, pointing to Ayo Dosunmu’s willingness to defend the length of the floor. “With Ayo picking up full court every day,” Ball said, describing the team’s preparation in his postgame presser . “You’ve got a lot of players on the team just going at each other, for real.” That is useful context for a group whose offseason has often been discussed in terms of pace, shooting and personality. The players describe a preparation process that also demanded consistent effort against one another. Finch saw another benefit from those sessions: players arrived ready to work. “I’ve never been around a team that we didn’t have to worry about getting anyone in shape this preseason,” he noted after the game. Conditioning alone will not win a rebounding battle. It does help a team sustain the movement, contact and repeated efforts required to compete. Rudy Gobert had help on the glass Credit: Matt Krohn-USA TODAY Sports Gobert did his part, collecting 15 rebounds, including five on offense. Yet Minnesota’s advantage extended beyond its starting center. Edwards grabbed 10 rebounds. Jaden McDaniels added eight. Joan Beringer collected six in fewer than 14 minutes, and Dosunmu contributed five, including three offensive boards. That distribution matters for a roster relying on more athleticism around Gobert. If the Wolves are going to hold up against bigger opponents, their guards and wings have to participate in finishing possessions. Wednesday provided a good example of what that can look like. Minnesota repeatedly created another opportunity after a miss while allowing Miami only four offensive rebounds. There is a distinction between playing smaller and accepting that the opponent will control the glass. The Wolves showed they can challenge that outcome through collective involvement. McDaniels described a similar mindset toward contact. “Just knowing that teams are going to try to be physical with us and then just embracing the physicality,” he added in the locker room. He also emphasized maintaining Minnesota’s own game while responding to the opponent. The Wolves do not need to abandon their faster approach every time a bigger team appears on the schedule. They need to support it with enough resistance and rebounding to keep playing it. Jonathan Kuminga gave Minnesota an important option Kuminga’s work against Antetokounmpo was another encouraging development. Finch singled him out afterward, praising his willingness to contest catches, meet Antetokounmpo early and keep applying his body throughout possessions. Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn-USA TODAY Sports “He just wasn’t afraid to put his body on him continually,” Finch said when explaining the matchup. Antetokounmpo still scored 35 points on 13-of-19 shooting. Minnesota did not erase his influence, and Kuminga was clear that stopping everything was never a realistic expectation. His explanation was straightforward: keep making the assignment difficult. “I won’t give up because we’re trying to win these games,” Kuminga said in his postgame interview . “We’re trying to establish something over here.” That persistence gives Finch something valuable as he works through his rotation. Minnesota needs players willing to accept demanding assignments without allowing an opponent’s success to dictate their effort on the next possession. The opener also left questions. The reserve frontcourt had difficult stretches, and Gobert cannot be expected to solve every matchup. Opponents will study the Wolves, test their depth and force adjustments. But Minnesota’s first answer deserves attention. Against a powerful Miami frontcourt, the Wolves competed through contact, dominated the offensive glass and received rebounding contributions throughout the rotation. The concerns about their size were reasonable. After Wednesday, treating physicality as an automatic weakness looks considerably less convincing. item.title: “Emotional To See” – Andre Agassi Reveals Why Alexander Zverev’s 2026 Success Despite Criticism Means So Much to Him
item.description: Jun 8, 2025; Paris, FR; Andre Agassi at the trophy presentation for the Carlos Alcaraz of Spain and Jannik Sinner of Italy men’s singles final match on day 15 at Roland Garros Stadium. © Susan Mullane-Imagn Images Tennis legend Andre Agassi recently expressed admiration for Alexander Zverev and explained why the German player’s 2026 feats matter. Zverev has had a breakthrough season, winning his first two career major titles at the French Open and the US Open. He saw off Flavio Cobolli 6–1, 4–6, 6–4, 6–7, 6–1 to clinch his first Major title at Roland Garros. He defeated the home favorite Ben Shelton 6–3, 7–6(2), 5–7, 6–2 on the Arthur Ashe Stadium to lift the US Open trophy. Zverev made a semifinal run at the Australian Open before being seen off by Carlos Alcaraz. He also reached the final at Wimbledon, where Jannik Sinner beat him 7–6(9), 6–7(2), 3–6, 4–6. Although Zverev faced criticism for winning titles in the absence of Alcaraz and Sinner, who were absent due to injuries or early exits, Andre Agassi appreciated the German tennis player. When asked about his favorite tennis moment of 2026 in an interview with Tennis Channel, the former World No. 1 highlighted Zverev’s feat, saying it was emotional to see his hard work finally pay off. “Oh God, you guys really put me on the spot. The story of this was Sascha getting over the line for his first Slam. That was his… that was, you know, emotional to see. Sascha is one of the hardest workers on the Tour and having that rewarded with finally achieving, you can’t help but feel good about it. Great to see Carlitos back, and I hope Sinner is using his time wisely because, you know, those two guys are so good for the game. So let’s hope for even better things in 2027.” Zverev’s French Open win made him the first German man to win a Grand Slam singles title in 30 years, since Boris Becker at the 1996 Australian Open. Andy Roddick reacts to Andre Agassi’s playful take on Alexander Zverev following the Laver Cup During the post-match speech at the 2026 Laver Cup, Andre Agassi took a light-hearted jab at Alexander Zverev, highlighting the latter’s first two career Grand Slam wins. “Congratulations, Sascha, on a crazy year,” Agassi said. “Seeing you win [a Grand Slam] for the first time, I know how important that was to you, and it was important to me too, because I could start listening to your press conferences again. You weren’t like, ‘Waah, why do I always lose? Why am I the third best in the world? I suck’. But then you win, and it’s like, ‘I’m only a one-time Slam champion; I’ve got to do it again.” Roddick praised Agassi’s ability to switch quickly from joking to expressing appreciation and highlighted his team’s love for him. “Andre [Agassi] has an unbelievable ability to shift gears very, very quickly. He can go from kind of roasting Zverev to having a very heartfelt moment to his team. His team loves playing for him; by the way, there is no doubt about it,” said Roddick. Team Europe, including Zve

The story of this was Sascha getting over the line for his first Slam. That was his… that was, you know, emotional to see. Sascha is one of the hardest workers on the Tour and having that rewarded with finally achieving, you can’t help but feel good about it. Great to see Carlitos back, and I hope Sinner is using his time wisely because, you know, those two guys are so good for the game. So let’s hope for even better things in 2027.” Zverev’s French Open win made him the first German man to win a Grand Slam singles title in 30 years, since Boris Becker at the 1996 Australian Open. Andy Roddick reacts to Andre Agassi’s playful take on Alexander Zverev following the Laver Cup During the post-match speech at the 2026 Laver Cup, Andre Agassi took a light-hearted jab at Alexander Zverev, highlighting the latter’s first two career Grand Slam wins. “Congratulations, Sascha, on a crazy year,” Agassi said. “Seeing you win [a Grand Slam] for the first time, I know how important that was to you, and it was important to me too, because I could start listening to your press conferences again. You weren’t like, ‘Waah, why do I always lose? Why am I the third best in the world? I suck’. But then you win, and it’s like, ‘I’m only a one-time Slam champion; I’ve got to do it again.” Roddick praised Agassi’s ability to switch quickly from joking to expressing appreciation and highlighted his team’s love for him. “Andre [Agassi] has an unbelievable ability to shift gears very, very quickly. He can go from kind of roasting Zverev to having a very heartfelt moment to his team. His team loves playing for him; by the way, there is no doubt about it,” said Roddick. Team Europe, including Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, Flavio Cobolli, Rafael Jodar, Jakub Mensik, and Casper Ruud, defeated Team World, which was led by Andre Agassi, 13-5 at the 2026 Laver Cup. item.title: Nottingham Forest’s false start places early focus on Glasner and Delap
item.description: Austrian’s tactics need adapting to but Forest are in the bottom three and their owner is not the patient type Sitting 19th in the Premier League was not the plan for Nottingham Forest after the arrival of a highly acclaimed manager and a £45m striker to fuel their ambitions. The fates of Oliver Glasner and Liam Delap are intertwined and with the stark stats of zero home goals and a solitary point at the City Ground: it is not the dream start they were aiming for. As Delap prepares to return to Ipswich, where his career ignited, on Friday night, Forest are remaining calm. There is a desperation to get away from the short-termism that caused so many problems; 12 months ago, they were on their third head coach of a disappointing season. This summer they were ruthless with the removal of Vítor Pereira, who had done a fine job to escape the drop, because they saw an opportunity to upgrade with Glasner, hoping he could transform Forest like he did Crystal Palace. Continue reading...

item.title: Marc Marquez retirement predicted if he wins tenth MotoGP world title
item.description: Marc Marquez could be just five races from retirement. That’s according to MotoGP race winner Marco Melandri, who thinks a tenth championship would be enough for the legend to call it quits. Marquez regularly spoke about his time in the sport coming to an end at the start of the season amid more injury troubles that culminated in a teary Le Mans exit and double surgery. Since then, he’s performed yet another remarkable title turnaround and is considered by most as the 2026 championship favourite. During that time there were two other key developments - Marquez signed a new contract, and got a new teammate for 2027 in the shape of Pedro Acosta . According to Melandri, that latter factor could play a huge part in what happens this winter. Pedro Acosta emerges as key factor in Marquez retirement prediction The five-time MotoGP race winner said: "For me, if Marquez wins his tenth World Championship, he could retire. "Nobody can know for sure. But Ducati needs a plan B, which it doesn't have right now. “Marquez knows that Acosta, his future teammate, can beat him. He's the first teammate who could achieve that, and it could happen. “Furthermore, he's following the political and regulatory changes brought about by Liberty Media, with their events and the new format. There are many factors in favour of him retiring if he wins tenth time.” Marquez signed a two-year extension with Ducati for 2027 and 2028, but it later emerged that it was a ‘1+1 deal’ meaning 2028 is an option both parties would speak about at the end of next season. Many think Acosta could push Marquez to retire (Credit: Red Bull Content Pool) Many think Acosta could push Marquez to retire (Credit: Red Bull Content Pool) Marquez's Ducati contract may not guarantee his long-term future Next year brings about a string of regulation changes, including smaller engines, less aerodynamics and Pirelli tyres. It also sees a record 22 events and the introduction of a second qualifying session, something Marquez has publicly criticised . He’s also spoken out against Liberty Media bringing in fines for riders who fail to show up for promotional events. Adding his voice to the complaints about the new rules, Marquez claimed they will bring forward the end of his career. Recently speaking about his future, the 33-year-old also suggested he could retire in the next few years. What Marquez has said about leaving MotoGP In an interview with MotoGP, he commented: "I'm here and competing because, for now, I haven't thrown in the towel mentally. "I've already achieved a lot, but I still feel competitive. And I know that, if I want to, I can remain competitive for a few more years. "But we're not in a sport like football or tennis, where you give 100 per cent, although the risk is much lower. "So, there are many factors to consider in MotoGP before retiring. item.title: Former WWE stars sign new 5-year AEW deal
item.description: Former WWE stars sign new 5-year AEW deal appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Earlier this year at AEW All In 2026, former WWE Superstars Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods made their All Elite Wrestling debut . Going with Kofi and Austin Creed, the duo made their debut in the Trios title match. Paired with Swerve Strickland, the three of them won the AEW Trios Championship before losing it to Adam Page, Bandido, and Brody King at AEW WrestleDream 2026. Now, Fightful Select has reported a major update on New Level’s [Kofi & Austin Creed] AEW contract. “New Level signed five-year AEW contracts,” Fightful Select said. According to the report, Kofi and Creed were pitched to join AEW and work with Strickland. It was also added that Strickland played a major role in bridging the relationship between the duo and AEW, as Tony Khan was hesitant to speak with them before their WWE contract was over. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Long before joining AEW as New Level, Creed and Kofi were known as The New Day in WWE. While popular babyface wrestlers almost throughout their careers, Kofi and Woods turned heel toward the final run of their careers. AEW’s New Level talk about their WWE salary paycut Just days after making their AEW debut, Kofi and Creed of The New Level appeared on The Ariel Helwani Show, where they opened up in detail about their alleged WWE pay cut. “Compensation was definitely a big part, but more so, we wanted to work. We wanted to go out there and showcase our skills and showcase our talents. We wanted to do what we love. We love going out there and messing with fans, threatening to ground kids, and really garner reactions to people, and send them home with incredible memories they’ll never forget. I don’t know exactly what’s out there. I will say, it was more than 50 percent, which a lot of people don’t know,” Kofi said.

item.title: Walker Kessler equals Wilt Chamberlain in historic Lakers 56-year feat vs. Warriors
item.description: Walker Kessler equals Wilt Chamberlain in historic Lakers 56-year feat vs. Warriors originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Panacea acquisitions are rare in the NBA. Teams sign many players to fill specific gaps, but they have their own weaknesses that eventually get exposed. Walker Kessler seems like a rare panacea signing for the Los Angeles Lakers . He helped Luka Doncic and JJ Redick get an opening night 127-105 win over the Golden State Warriors . More than that, he was also the best big man on the floor. It was proven when he matched an insane record by Wilt Chamberlain. Kessler gets historic NBA feat achieved by Chamberlain in Lakers vs. Warriors The Lakers had a lot of holes to fix during the NBA offseason. Coach JJ Redick had to build schemes around Luka Doncic without LeBron James on the roster. They also lost big men like Jaxson Hayes and Deandre Ayton. So the natural solution was to find someone who could fill all those holes at once. This is where Walker Kessler comes in. On paper, he is the perfect player to slot alongside Doncic and complement Coach Redick's schemes. When the Lakers faced the Warriors, it was time to put those skills and ideas into practice. Kessler delivered. Coach Redick gave him 30 minutes to anchor the Lakers' defense and serve as the perfect big man to help Doncic. How great was his Lakers debut? Kessler finished with 26 points on 100% from the field. He also got an assist. Defensively, Coach Redick saw him grab nine rebounds while snagging two blocks. Kessler's 100% from the field wasn't just a great Lakers debut; it also matched a record only Wilt Chamberlain came close to. The new Lakers big man went 12-for-12 from the field. Only Chamberlain finished with more in his 14-for-14 game on March 11, 1969, against the Detroit Pistons , via ESPN Insights. Walker Kessler Lakers Debut. 26 PTS, 9 REB, 2 BLK, 12/12 FG, 95 TS% League really let Luka get a center 😭 https://t.co/fIdC082M2h — Basketball Performances (@NBAPerformances) October 22, 2026 Coach Redick had expectations about Kessler and how he fits in with the Lakers too, via Dan Woike of The Athletic. “I think he wants to embrace that. I think that’s why he wanted to be a Laker. And why he wanted to be here was because of the fact that there are stakes every single night when you wear a Lakers uniform. We’ve had a number of conversations. We had a long conversation the other day about it. I think the awareness is there; how you navigate that early on and how you navigate that in your first year, there’s no way to predict that because you’ve never dealt with it before. By the end, Coach Redick and the Lakers seem to have found the perfect running mate for Doncic. The Lakers superstar also scored 28 points of his own, and it all got easier with Kessler manning the paint. All of this helped the Lakers get their first win of the season. item.title: Milwaukee Bucks’ Myles Turner sends clear message to the team after first loss vs. Washington Wizards
item.description: Myles Turner doubled down on Taylor Jenkins’ take about the Milwaukee Bucks’ 128-116 road loss to the Washington Wizards on Wednesday, saying the game was a huge learning experience for the team, which is currently in its rebuilding phase. Turner felt the Milwaukee Bucks missed a golden opportunity to notch their first win of the 2026-27 campaign, especially since they led most of the game. Milwaukee built a 96-90 lead early in the fourth quarter before Washington went on a 21-2 run to shift the momentum. What Myles Turner said about the Milwaukee Bucks’ opener vs. Washington Wizards Oct 21, 2026; Washington, District of Columbia, USA; Washington Wizards guard Trae Young (3) shoots the ball as Milwaukee Bucks center Myles Turner (3) defends in the first half at Capital One Arena. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Myles Turner is embracing his veteran leadership role with the Milwaukee Bucks. After Wednesday’s loss, he urged his teammates to continue developing good habits that will eventually translate to on-court success. “My message to the team after the game was, fellas, from the first preseason game to where we’re at now, we’ve gotten a lot better,” Turner said. “And one of the things I hate that people say, but it’s true, is that ‘It’s a long season.’ Yeah, it’s the first game, but if you keep looking at it like, ‘ Hey, it’s a long season, you feel like, ‘OK, we’ll get there eventually.’ That’s not really our mindset. Obviously, we’re building and want to get better every single night, but I think we took a step in the right direction tonight.” Tyler Herro sticks to the positives in the Milwaukee Bucks’ performance Tyler Herro led the Milwaukee Bucks with 24 points, nine assists, and four three-pointers on 9-for-21 shooting in his official debut for his hometown team. After the game, the one-time All-Star lauded the team’s willingness to share the rock, as they had 28 assists on 41 field goals made. “I thought we moved the ball well at times. It got a little sticky, I think, when they went on a run a little bit… I think when we were under control and getting the ball to where it needs to go, and then guys were just playing the right way and making the right decisions, we got the shots we wanted,” Herro said. item.title: Harry Kane admits wait to learn if he has won Ballon d’Or is ‘very stressful’ for family
item.description: Bayern Munich and England striker is odds-on favourite ‘I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to’ Harry Kane would love to know now whether he has won the Ballon d’Or because the uncertainty and constant questions are driving his family to distraction. But the Bayern Munich and England striker accepts the suspense before the big reveal at the London Palladium on Monday night is part of the show. Kane is the odds-on favourite to win the prestigious individual honour after a prolific run of form. The 33-year-old scored 61 goals for Bayern last season and 12 for England. This time out, he has 10 for Bayern and six for England. He scored from the penalty spot in Wednesday night’s 2-2 Champions League draw against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena, although his stand-out moment was the inch-perfect through ball that set up Alphonso Davies to make it 1-1. Continue reading...

item.title: Shola Ameobi: ‘I thought: how can I be most useful to Newcastle? Then the cog started turning’
item.description: From experiencing racism growing up in Newcastle to becoming a derby hero and now a member of the executive team, the former striker has been on a remarkable journey “There were times where I feared for my life as a kid, being harassed and chased by different groups of people,” Shola Ameobi says. “There were situations where I had to sprint to get away from groups of lads who didn’t like me because of what I looked like.” Ameobi is recalling growing up in Newcastle during the late 1980s and 1990s, having moved from Nigeria aged six. There were, he says, “lots of moments” like that. “It was almost as if I had to hide myself to be able to do what I love to do. It wasn’t a very nice feeling, having to worry about getting from A to B. It was just part of my world. I had to be more aware of my surroundings and what I was doing.” Continue reading...

item.title: History comes home as St Louis City top Columbus Crew to win US Open Cup
item.description: Title is club’s first-ever since 2023 founding St Louis clubs have won 11 Open Cups all-time Daniel Edelman nets winner in 5-4 win on penalties For much of the 20th century, winning the US Open Cup required a team to beat someone from St Louis. The Gateway City was home to many of the nation’s best teams during some ramshackle eras of soccer in the United States, with six different clubs combining for 10 trophy lifts. The most recent came in 1988, when St Louis Busch Seniors beat San Francisco-based Greek-American AC in the last throes of a tournament history dominated by amateur and semi-pro teams. MLS has won every Open Cup but one since starting play in 1996, and St Louis didn’t have an MLS club until 2023. From the beginning, club figures spoke of aims to restore the city to soccer prominence. Well, mission accomplished. St Louis City are US Open Cup champions, outlasting the Columbus Crew 5-4 on penalties to end the city’s 38-year wait for a major US soccer title and earn a place in the field for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. Continue reading...

item.title: Arsenal’s Declan Rice strikes late to deny Bayern Munich after Harry Kane penalty
item.description: It is as if Harry Kane cannot get enough of tormenting Arsenal. The Bayern Munich striker has plenty of form from his Tottenham days. He remains the top scorer in north London derby history with 14 goals. He made an impact yet again here and yet it was not a night when he had the final word. That honour fell to Declan Rice, the Arsenal midfielder storming into the Bayern area in the 82nd minute to guide home a low finish that Kane would have been proud to call his own. Arsenal were hunting their latest statement result. Only once had they ever won away against Bayern – the 2-0 in the Champions League last 16 second leg in 2013, although it did not prevent an away goals exit. Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player that night. When Eberechi Eze, who came on for the injured Bukayo Saka in the 10th minute, gave them the lead midway through the first half, their hopes surged. Continue reading...

item.title: Barkley and Buendía on target as Aston Villa sink Viking to maintain perfect start
item.description: For a little over 20 minutes, Aston Villa could look down on the rest of Europe. They had scaled the Champions League summit on goal difference when Henrik Heggheim put through his own net and the fact was not lost on the Holte End, who reflected their position in song and perhaps allowed themselves another glimpse back to the days when their supremacy was undisputed. “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more,” the pre-match tifo display had read. Perhaps Villa really will rekindle the spirit of 1982 but the frustration here, albeit minor in the wider scheme, was that they could not maintain their bird’s-eye view over the continent. A superbly taken volley by Peter Christiansen, awarded by the video assistant referee after initially being disallowed for offside, gave Viking a consolation their second-half display deserved and meant Unai Emery’s side must make do with slumming it just behind Paris Saint-Germain. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Champions League drama galore – so why do we feel hollow?
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Now then, which one of you hipsters decided to put Porto 0-1 PSV on? Oh dear. This was another night of Bigger Cup at its Bigliest self, comebacks everywhere, 40 goals in nine games, six of those in a best-v-best clash as Paris Saint-Germain rallied late against Barcelona. Even in defeat, Lamine Yamal found space to decorate the room with a ludicrous toe-poke equaliser, and there was a wholesome tale in Italy as Scott McTominay scored twice for Napoli in their 4-3 win against Bodø/Glimt. These were his first strikes since returning from heart surgery, taking his tally at the club to 29 goals in 86 appearances. No wonder Erik ten Hag was peeved with his bosses at Manchester United for shipping the midfielder off to Naples. One has to admire the courage of Erik ten Hag, speaking out on Man United’s ‘toxic culture’ [yesterday’s Football Daily, full email edition]. I broke out in a cold sweat reading about how they ‘give power to the players’. The stuff of nightmares, really” – Rowan Sweeney. Roberto De Zerbi wants Spurs to be a family ( yesterday’s Football Daily )? And he thinks playing for or with a family will avoid relegation? Well, I have this uncle. He’s called Weird Uncle Fiver (now there’s a throwback – Football Daily Ed), and he loves to [snip – Football Daily lawyers, and time-travelling pedants]” – Mike Wilner. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Donald McRae
item.content:encoded: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: My old teammate Miroslav Klose is bucking a trend in German coaching | Philipp Lahm
item.description: ‘Miro’, now in charge at Nürnberg, knows the value of consistency and identity in an era of tinkering coaches who did not play professionally You learn the most from the best. The Champions League winners are Paris Saint-Germain, and they could achieve a historic hat-trick this season. Since the tournament’s rebrand in 1992, they would be only the second club to accomplish this feat, after Real Madrid’s run from 2016 to 2018. I see clear parallels between the two. For Madrid, nine players started in all three of their final victories. Similarly, PSG won their two finals with virtually identical lineups. The only change came during their title defence in Budapest , where Gianluigi Donnarumma no longer featured in goal, Luis Enrique having parted ways with the Italian European champion. core players: about 70 to 85% each remaining regular starters: 50 to 60% each squad players: 40 to 45% each fringe squad places: sharing the remaining maximum of 20% Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...
